_about: Hand-written key points for pyt-pharmacology.html (27 Nov 2026, lead). One short note per previous-year topic, plus one sample question id from the bank (FMGE recalls only, no images) and a one-line why. pyt_pages.py reads this; topic names, ranks and counts come from study.db.
subject: Pharmacology
intro: Pharmacology in FMGE is mostly the same few ideas asked again: drug of choice, the classic adverse effect, the antidote, and one or two mechanisms per drug group. These are the topics that keep coming back, most-asked first, with the one thing to remember about each.

ph.gen.pk.note: Clearance = 0.693 × Vd ÷ t½. Steady state takes 4–5 half-lives, whatever the dose. Loading dose depends on Vd; maintenance dose on clearance. High first-pass drugs (nitroglycerin, lidocaine, propranolol) have low oral bioavailability.

ph.gen.pd.note: Potency = how much drug you need (position of the curve); efficacy = the maximum effect it can reach (height of the curve). A competitive antagonist shifts the curve right without lowering the maximum; a non-competitive one lowers the maximum. Therapeutic index = TD50 ÷ ED50.
ph.gen.pd.why: The ceiling of the dose-response curve is efficacy; potency only tells you the dose needed.

ph.gen.enz.note: Inducers: rifampicin, phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbitone, smoking (CYP1A2), chronic alcohol. Inhibitors: macrolides, azoles, ciprofloxacin, cimetidine, valproate, grapefruit, acute alcohol. Exams ask the result: an inhibitor raises the other drug's level (toxicity), an inducer lowers it (failure).
ph.gen.enz.why: Smoking induces CYP1A2, which clears clozapine. Stopping smoking removes the induction, clozapine levels rise, and seizures follow.

ph.ans.chol.note: Neostigmine reverses non-depolarising block and does not cross into the brain; physostigmine does (atropine poisoning). Atropine is first-line for symptomatic bradycardia. Anticholinergic toxicity: hot, dry, red, blind, mad.
ph.ans.chol.why: Neostigmine raises acetylcholine at the motor end plate, which out-competes the non-depolarising blocker.

ph.ans.adr.note: α1 = vasoconstriction (why adrenaline is added to local anaesthetics), β1 = heart, β2 = bronchodilation. Adrenaline is the drug of choice in anaphylaxis (IM). Tamsulosin (α1A-selective) for BPH causes first-dose postural hypotension.
ph.ans.adr.why: Adrenaline constricts local vessels through α1 receptors, so less bleeding and slower washout of the anaesthetic.

ph.ans.bb.note: Non-selective β-blockers (propranolol, timolol) are avoided in asthma. Propranolol is first-line for migraine prophylaxis, performance anxiety and thyrotoxic symptoms. β-blocker overdose: give glucagon, which raises cAMP without β receptors.
ph.ans.bb.why: Glucagon acts on its own receptor to raise cAMP in the heart, bypassing the blocked β receptors.

ph.ans.op.note: Organophosphates block acetylcholinesterase irreversibly: muscarinic signs (salivation, sweating, bronchorrhoea, miosis, bradycardia) plus nicotinic weakness. Atropine is given first and titrated to dry secretions; pralidoxime reactivates the enzyme only before it 'ages'.
ph.ans.op.why: Atropine blocks the muscarinic receptors flooded with acetylcholine; it does not help the nicotinic weakness.

ph.ans.mg.note: Antibodies against nicotinic ACh receptors: ptosis and fatigable weakness that worsens through the day. Pyridostigmine is the mainstay for symptoms; edrophonium (Tensilon) was the classic diagnostic test. Watch aminoglycosides, which worsen myasthenia.
ph.ans.mg.why: Pyridostigmine inhibits acetylcholinesterase, so more acetylcholine reaches the reduced number of receptors.

ph.ans.gl.note: Prostaglandin analogues (latanoprost) are first-line for open-angle glaucoma: more uveoscleral outflow, once daily, darkens the iris. Timolol reduces aqueous production but can trigger asthma by systemic absorption. Pilocarpine and acetazolamide for acute angle closure.
ph.ans.gl.why: Timolol is a non-selective β-blocker; drops absorbed through the nasolacrimal duct block β2 receptors in the lungs.

ph.ans.pheo.note: Alpha-blockade first (phenoxybenzamine), beta-blocker only afterwards. A β-blocker alone leaves α vasoconstriction unopposed and can cause a hypertensive crisis. Diagnosis: plasma free or urinary metanephrines.
ph.ans.pheo.why: Alpha first, then beta: unopposed α stimulation is the danger of starting with a β-blocker.

ph.amb.tb.note: Know each first-line drug's signature adverse effect: isoniazid neuropathy (give pyridoxine) and hepatitis, rifampicin orange secretions and enzyme induction, pyrazinamide hyperuricaemia and hepatitis, ethambutol optic neuritis (red-green colour vision). New drug-sensitive TB: 2 months HRZE, then 4 months HRE.
ph.amb.tb.why: Drug-sensitive pulmonary TB starts with four drugs, isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide and ethambutol, in the intensive phase.

ph.amb.abx.note: High-yield pairs: MSSA, cloxacillin; MRSA, vancomycin; SBP, cefotaxime; aminoglycosides, nephro- and ototoxicity; fluoroquinolones, tendon rupture; macrolides, QT prolongation; metronidazole with alcohol, a disulfiram-like reaction.
ph.amb.abx.why: Oxacillin-sensitive Staph aureus is MSSA, and a penicillinase-resistant penicillin (cloxacillin) is the drug of choice.

ph.amb.art.note: Tenofovir: renal toxicity (Fanconi syndrome) and bone loss. Zidovudine: anaemia. Abacavir: hypersensitivity (HLA-B*5701). Efavirenz: vivid dreams. Tenofovir and lamivudine also treat hepatitis B.
ph.amb.art.why: Tenofovir damages the proximal tubule, giving Fanconi syndrome: glycosuria, phosphaturia and aminoaciduria.

ph.cvs.htn.note: ACE inhibitors: dry cough and angioedema (bradykinin), avoid in pregnancy. Pregnancy: labetalol, nifedipine, methyldopa. Hypertensive emergency: lower the pressure gradually with IV drugs such as labetalol, nicardipine or nitroprusside. Never combine an ACE inhibitor with sacubitril.
ph.cvs.htn.why: Hypertensive encephalopathy needs controlled IV lowering; IV labetalol is a standard first choice.

ph.cvs.hf.note: Drugs that reduce death in heart failure with reduced EF: ACE inhibitor, ARB or ARNI (sacubitril-valsartan), β-blocker, spironolactone, SGLT2 inhibitor. Digoxin and loop diuretics relieve symptoms only. Stop an ACE inhibitor 36 hours before starting sacubitril-valsartan.
ph.cvs.hf.why: Neprilysin and ACE both break down bradykinin; blocking both at once lets bradykinin build up and causes angioedema.

ph.cvs.arr.note: Adenosine stops SVT (very short-acting). Amiodarone: pulmonary fibrosis, thyroid problems, corneal deposits. Torsades de pointes: give IV magnesium sulfate. Many drugs prolong QT: class IA and III antiarrhythmics, macrolides, antipsychotics.
ph.cvs.arr.why: Adenosine briefly blocks the AV node, breaking the re-entry circuit that keeps SVT going.

ph.cns.aed.note: Drug of choice is asked by seizure type: absence, ethosuximide or valproate; infantile spasms, ACTH, but vigabatrin in tuberous sclerosis; status epilepticus, IV lorazepam first. Valproate is teratogenic (neural tube defects). Phenytoin causes gum hypertrophy and hirsutism.
ph.cns.aed.why: Ash-leaf spots point to tuberous sclerosis, where vigabatrin is the first choice for infantile spasms.

ph.cns.park.note: Levodopa is given with carbidopa (a peripheral decarboxylase inhibitor). COMT inhibitors extend each dose: entacapone works peripherally only, tolcapone peripherally and centrally (liver toxicity). Typical antipsychotics and metoclopramide cause drug-induced parkinsonism.
ph.cns.park.why: Tolcapone crosses the blood-brain barrier, so it inhibits COMT in both places; entacapone does not.

ph.cns.apsy.note: Clozapine is for treatment-resistant schizophrenia: agranulocytosis (blood counts), seizures, myocarditis. Typical antipsychotics: dystonia, akathisia, parkinsonism, tardive dyskinesia, NMS (treat with dantrolene or bromocriptine). Olanzapine: weight gain.
ph.cns.apsy.why: Clozapine's agranulocytosis is idiosyncratic, not dose-related, which is why blood counts are monitored.

ph.cns.adep.note: SSRIs are first-line for depression and anxiety. TCA overdose: anticholinergic signs, wide QRS and arrhythmias; treat with sodium bicarbonate. Serotonin syndrome: hyperthermia, clonus, agitation. MAO inhibitors with tyramine-rich food: the cheese reaction.
ph.cns.adep.why: Sodium bicarbonate reverses the cardiac sodium-channel block of TCAs and narrows the QRS.

ph.endo.dm.note: Metformin: lactic acidosis, B12 deficiency, no hypoglycaemia. SGLT2 inhibitors (-gliflozins): genital fungal infections, euglycaemic ketoacidosis. Glitazones: fluid retention and heart failure. Sulfonylureas and insulin: hypoglycaemia. GLP-1 agonists: weight loss, pancreatitis.
ph.endo.dm.why: SGLT2 inhibitors put glucose in the urine, which feeds recurrent genital candidiasis.

ph.endo.ster.note: Long-term steroids: Cushingoid features, osteoporosis, hyperglycaemia, cataract, adrenal suppression. Never stop them suddenly; taper. Dexamethasone has no mineralocorticoid effect; fludrocortisone is mostly mineralocorticoid.
ph.endo.ster.why: Moon face and central obesity come from too much glucocorticoid receptor stimulation.

ph.chemo.mab.note: Learn the target of each '-mab': trastuzumab, HER2 (cardiotoxic); rituximab, CD20; bevacizumab, VEGF; infliximab and adalimumab, TNF-α (screen for latent TB first); cetuximab, EGFR.

ph.chemo.tki.note: Imatinib blocks BCR-ABL (chronic myeloid leukaemia) and c-KIT (GIST). The '-tinibs' each have a target: gefitinib and erlotinib, EGFR; sunitinib, multiple kinases including VEGFR.

ph.haem.ac.note: Heparin is monitored with aPTT and reversed with protamine; warfarin with INR, reversed with vitamin K, plus prothrombin complex or FFP for bleeding. Rivaroxaban and apixaban block factor Xa; dabigatran blocks thrombin. Warfarin skin necrosis happens in protein C deficiency.
ph.haem.ac.why: Warfarin lowers protein C before the clotting factors, so the blood is briefly prothrombotic; skin necrosis follows in protein C deficiency.

ph.resp.asthma.note: Salbutamol (SABA) for quick relief; inhaled steroids are the controller. Montelukast for aspirin-sensitive and exercise asthma. Theophylline has a narrow therapeutic window, and CYP1A2 inhibitors such as ciprofloxacin make it toxic.
ph.resp.asthma.why: An inhaled short-acting β2 agonist is the fastest bronchodilator.

ph.resp.copd.note: Long-acting bronchodilators are the base: tiotropium (a LAMA) and LABAs. Inhaled steroids are added for frequent exacerbations or high eosinophils. Oxygen therapy and stopping smoking are what improve survival.

ph.git.eme.note: Ondansetron (5-HT3) for chemotherapy vomiting; it prolongs QT. Metoclopramide crosses into the brain and causes dystonia; domperidone does not. Aprepitant (NK1) for delayed chemotherapy vomiting. Motion sickness: hyoscine.
ph.git.eme.why: Metoclopramide blocks D2 receptors in the basal ganglia and can cause an acute dystonic reaction.

ph.ae.note: The classic pairs: ethambutol, optic neuritis; isoniazid, neuropathy; amiodarone, pulmonary fibrosis; ACE inhibitors, cough; clozapine, agranulocytosis; vincristine, neuropathy; cyclophosphamide, haemorrhagic cystitis; bleomycin, lung fibrosis; doxorubicin, cardiomyopathy.

ph.antid.note: Paracetamol, N-acetylcysteine; opioids, naloxone; benzodiazepines, flumazenil; organophosphates, atropine and pralidoxime; heparin, protamine; warfarin, vitamin K; methanol, fomepizole; iron, deferoxamine; magnesium toxicity, calcium gluconate; β-blockers, glucagon; TCAs, sodium bicarbonate.
ph.antid.why: Lost reflexes and slow breathing mean magnesium toxicity: stop the infusion and give IV calcium gluconate.
